overview: This Senate resolution marks the 50th anniversary of the sinking of the SS Edmund Fitzgerald, a large iron-ore freighter that went down in Lake Superior during a severe storm on November 10, 1975, killing all 29 crew members. It notes that the Coast Guard's investigation led to safety changes on the Great Lakes, including weather-monitoring buoys, and that the wreck was remembered in Gordon Lightfoot's well-known song. It offers support to the crew's families, commends the rescue crews and the Coast Guard, and reaffirms a commitment to safe shipping on the Great Lakes. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on November 10, 2025. It is commemorative and does not change any law or spending.
for: Supporters say the resolution honors the lost crew and their families and recognizes the safety improvements that came from the tragedy.
against: Critics say the resolution is commemorative and does not change any law or spending.
